trust_decision.summary: On a redirect, HttpExecutor.prepareRedirectUrlOptions decides whether credential headers may follow to the new origin; at the pinned commit it only strips the exact lowercase `authorization` key, so PRIVATE-TOKEN, `Authorization`, X-Api-Key etc. are forwarded cross-origin. Under Electron the decision only runs when the request uses redirect:"manual".

landing_point.why: The summary names builder-util-runtime, cross-origin redirect and Authorization; prepareRedirectUrlOptions is the only redirect-strip function and line 323 checks only `headers?.authorization`.

AppUpdater.checkForUpdates with provider: gitlab (new createRequestOptions override forcing redirect:"manual", fix.diff:329-333)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Once prepareRedirectUrlOptions strips PRIVATE-TOKEN case-insensitively, the unit tests through the static helper pass, and the code comments say 'Electron net handles redirects automatically' (DifferentialDownloader.ts:238, multipleRangeDownloader.ts:124), so a solver can argue the provider/request-mode layer is outside the redirect-strip fix.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Same-origin redirects and the http->https same-host upgrade must keep PRIVATE-TOKEN/Authorization, and non-credential headers (User-Agent, Accept, range) must survive cross-origin redirects; an over-broad fix that drops all headers or strips on every redirect breaks GitLab/private-GitHub asset downloads.
